arguments.value: Use HTB with a root class at 100mbit and create per-client classes dynamically (10 max). You need a classifier that distinguishes each downloading client by IP/connection, because tc cannot automatically split bandwidth equally among an unknown set of clients by itself. Put all clients into equal-share leaf classes using SFQ/FQ_CoDel under a parent HTB class, and assign each client a class with rate 10mbit and ceil 100mbit (or a minimum guaranteed rate of 10mbit, depending on your requirement). Then use iptables/nftables marks or u32/flower filters to map each client to its own class. With only 10 clients, the practical solution is to create 10 classes and assign each active client to one class; HTB will let a lone client burst up to 100mbit, while multiple active classes will compete and each get approximately an equal share subject to the 10mbit guarantees. If you need automatic per-flow fairness without per-client class management, use fq_codel/cake instead of tc HTB.
